stem.en: Two boxes tied by a string are pulled by a force F. We treat the two boxes and the string as one system. Why can we leave out the tension in the string?

text.en: The tension in a tight string is zero.

feedback.en: A tight string does pull on both boxes. Tension is not zero.

text.en: The tension acts only on the floor.

feedback.en: The tension acts on the two boxes, not on the floor.

text.en: The tension is an internal force. Its two forces act inside the system, so they do not change the motion of the whole.

feedback.en: Right. Only external forces, like F, change the motion of the system.

explanation.en: Tension is an internal force: the string pulls Box 1 back and Box 2 forward with equal forces, both inside the system. Only external forces change the motion of the whole system.

hints.en: Is the string inside the system or outside it?
